Visual Reference Report · 01—08

Texture over time.

Eight references translated into a coherent live-visual language for Imaginary Lands—an ambient-techno world built from memory, material, atmosphere, physical phenomena and human trace.

Ambient TechnoLive VisualsiPhone CaptureAnalog TextureVisual Bible
The central observation These works do not depend on events. They hold attention through continuous, low-frequency change: light drifts, liquid flows, focus wanders, grain breathes.
01 · Synthesis

A world, not a content feed.

The references converge around restraint. Rather than filling the screen, they create objects and atmospheres that can be contemplated. The strongest direction for Imaginary Lands combines three sources.

A · Archive

Places actually lived

Paris windows, Taipei transit, hotel rooms, train platforms, sea, roads and weather. Personal footage gives the project a history no stock library can imitate.

B · Phenomena

Matter behaving in time

Water, fog, soap film, ice, ink, reflections, shadow and light. These images have no plot, yet remain endlessly watchable.

C · Human Trace

Presence without identity

Bodies appear as fragments, blur, reflected skin, gestures and residual energy—not as performers demanding narrative attention.

70% lived footage + 30% treatmentA more distinctive identity than 100% generated imagery.
02 · Atlas

Eight routes into the same terrain.

Each reference contributes a different visual function. Together they move from personal memory to sculptural abstraction, then return to lived human presence.

Ref · 01

Ariana Grande

Memory as soft, breathing material.

IntimacyFragilityNatureAnalog Archive
Imaginary Lands5 / 5
Creative Direction

A found reel of private memory

Emotion matters more than information. The work feels discovered rather than announced: a faded home movie in which nature, faces and darkness carry intimacy.

Visual Vocabulary

Faces, flora, light

  • Flowers, leaves, hands and eyes
  • Darkness, shadow and light spots
  • Silver-print monochrome
  • Grain, halation, bloom, soft focus
Motion Language

Float rather than travel

Subtle handheld drift resembles breathing or Super 8. Wind moves flowers, leaves and hair. Cross-dissolves, double exposure and opacity fades create continuity.

Rhythm

Emotion sync—not beat sync

Visual change often arrives one or two seconds before or after a musical shift. Long images are allowed to resonate; transitions follow emotional pressure rather than percussion.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Mostly real footage, lightly transformed

An estimated live-action base, with After Effects overlays, double exposure, opacity animation, grain and glow; restrained monochrome grading in DaVinci or Premiere.

Technical2 / 5Aesthetic4 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

Build a shared-memory layer

Shoot flowers, water, trees, faces, windows and sunlight at 60 fps. Retiming to 24 fps creates a gentle 40% slow motion. Add grain, bloom, light leaks and long opacity blends; introduce maps, scans, stone and restrained digital artifacts.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

Highly feasible

Light, framing and treatment matter more than the camera body. For Imaginary Lands, expand the personal home movie into shared memory: cities, landscapes, archives and the Paris–Taiwan axis.

Keep: slow pacing, floating camera, film texture and double exposure. Avoid: making nostalgia the entire concept.

Ref · 02

Rival Consoles

A sculptural object held in darkness.

MonolithGeometryNegative SpaceLight
Imaginary Lands5 / 5
Creative Direction

Presence without narrative

The image does not tell a story; it makes an object exist onstage. Architecture, absence and material weight invite sustained attention.

Visual Vocabulary

Black, planes, surfaces

  • Triangles, lines and sloped faces
  • Stone, concrete, metal, matte plastic
  • Large fields of negative space
  • Light as the true protagonist
Motion Language

Lighting design as animation

Light cuts, scans and disappears. Shadow occludes; forms rotate or reveal themselves slowly. Motion is sparse, but every change carries mass.

Rhythm

The courage to stop

Long holds give the audience time to inspect the form before the next slow reveal. This patience translates directly to ambient-techno pacing.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Clean 3D with restrained compositing

Most likely Blender/Cycles or Cinema 4D/Redshift, with After Effects used for grain and glow. Consistent geometry and lighting make heavy AI involvement unlikely.

Technical3 / 5Aesthetic5 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

One form, one light, one decision

Create a single sculptural object, place one area light, animate a slow rotation or light sweep, then add minimal grain and glow. A physical miniature and moving light could substitute for 3D.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

Useful as a capture tool, not the whole pipeline

An iPhone can record real textures, shadows or miniatures, but the core precision is easier in 3D. Merge its geometry with organic memory: a flower becoming sculpture, a rock becoming landscape, a tree becoming shadow.

Keep: black space, weight and rare motion. Avoid: an entirely cold, hard-geometric show.

Ref · 03

Moonvoid

Perception suspended at a threshold.

MistDecayDissolutionAmbiguity
Imaginary Lands4 / 5
Creative Direction

Between visible and invisible

The image lives between real and abstract, natural and digital, object and light. Its power comes from delaying recognition.

Visual Vocabulary

The medium is the subject

  • Water, haze and backlight
  • Blurred built structures
  • Reflection and shadow
  • Fog, glass, dirty lens, defocus
Motion Language

Material changes, not objects

The camera drifts almost imperceptibly. Light flows, focus migrates, fog changes density and water deforms. The movement belongs to the medium.

Rhythm

Stay inside one atmosphere

Slower even than the Ariana reference, shots can persist without clear sectional change. The space remains; only its visibility evolves.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Live action degraded into perception

Likely iPhone, DV, VHS, MiniDV or a small Sony camera; finished with blur, bloom, grain, curves and palette restriction. Heavy CG or generative traces are not evident.

Technical1 / 5Aesthetic4 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

Shoot through something

Film through steamed glass, water, scratched plastic or a deliberately dirty lens. Use hard backlight, allow focus to drift, lower resolution selectively, then limit the grade to two or three families of tone.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

Extremely feasible

The phone is well suited to found atmosphere and imperfect media. Use this language as interstitial space between more legible archive images, preserving ambiguity without removing every visual anchor.

Keep: opacity, uncertainty and slow density shifts. Avoid: an entire set with nothing recognizable.

Ref · 04

Floating Points

A physical phenomenon large enough to become a world.

FluidSurface TensionIridescenceEmergence
Imaginary Lands5 / 5
Creative Direction

The microscopic becomes monumental

Rather than describe a world, the work observes chemistry and surface tension until an ordinary material becomes an alien landscape.

Visual Vocabulary

Almost nothing—seen deeply

  • Liquid and fluid texture
  • Iridescent gradients
  • Black voids, ripples and bubbles
  • No people, architecture or plot
Motion Language

The camera waits; matter moves

A nearly locked camera lets the liquid generate non-repeating motion. Because the physics never resolve identically, the footage avoids a synthetic loop feel.

Rhythm

Gaze, do not cut

There is almost no edit, transition or story. The audience’s attention shifts toward detail—an ideal low-event visual condition for ambient music.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Practical macro capture

Probably soap film, or oil and water under polarized or angled LED light. Post-production may be limited to crop, contrast and color.

Technical1 / 5Aesthetic5 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

Build a tabletop phenomena lab

Use a glass vessel, soap solution or oil and water, controlled LED angles and a macro lens. Record long sessions, then select the moments with the richest slow emergence. Do less in post.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

Highly feasible with a macro attachment

Create a second library beside the travel archive: soap film, water, ink, milk, ice, fire, fog and light. These are not transitions or filler; they are autonomous contemplative subjects.

Keep: real physics and patient observation. Avoid: over-editing the phenomenon into a VJ loop.

Ref · 05

Zayn

Memory does not play continuously. It pulses.

ExposureProjectorReplacementMicro-Stimulation
Imaginary Lands5 / 5
Creative Direction

Instability as remembrance

The defining idea is not fast cutting, but an image that brightens, dims and briefly changes as memory does. Time itself becomes textured.

Visual Vocabulary

Four layers of flicker

  • Exposure breathing
  • Animated grain density
  • Two-to-four-frame image replacement
  • 16mm-like light-leak sweeps
Motion Language

Change inside the frame

The apparent motion often comes from luminance and texture rather than camera travel. A nearly still image remains alive through irregular temporal modulation.

Rhythm

Low-frequency attention cues

Subtle changes every one or two seconds create micro-stimulation without EDM-style impact. Occasional 2–4 frame substitutions behave like involuntary flashes of recollection.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Simple tools, precise timing

After Effects or an equivalent editor can animate exposure, grain and overlays rapidly. The technical setup is straightforward; the challenge is shaping irregularity without creating visual fatigue.

Technical2 / 5Aesthetic4 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

Build several flicker voices

Create separate film, CRT, projector, sensor, random-exposure and noise-only treatments. Map their intensity loosely—not literally—to filter movement, spectral density or vocal breath.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

Completely feasible

A simple shot of a Paris window can be transformed with exposure breathing, animated grain, bloom and blur. The value lies not in generating a new image, but in altering the temporal quality of a real one.

Keep: flicker as an instrument. Avoid: rigid beat sync or high-intensity flashing.

Ref · 06

Emma

Someone was here—yet no identity is fixed.

PresenceClub MemoryBodiesGhost
Imaginary Lands5 / 5
Creative Direction

Human energy as residual trace

People enter the visual world without becoming characters. The work captures proof of presence—ephemeral, anonymous and projected into by the viewer.

Visual Vocabulary

Bodies, never portraits

  • Hands, shoulders, hair and cropped heads
  • Skin reflecting in darkness
  • Occlusion, blur and partial framing
  • Underexposure and crushed black
Motion Language

Fast through proximity

The pace comes from handheld camera movement—crowd pressure, body sway and close distance—not merely from short edits. The viewer feels physically inside the room.

Rhythm

The space breathes with the light

A hand rises; the room flashes; darkness returns; time pauses. Live lighting creates a naturally variable rhythm with more authenticity than a uniform post effect.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Observational live action

Almost certainly practical capture. High-ISO noise, motion blur, compression and heavy black levels are design material, not defects. Position inside the crowd matters more than equipment.

Technical1 / 5Aesthetic4 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

Shoot ten minutes; keep thirty seconds

Enter the environment, remain close and let accidental gestures happen. Preserve imperfect focus and exposure. Edit for rare moments when light passes through a body rather than for complete actions.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

Ideal for iPhone capture

Use passing shoulders on platforms, hands at the edge of frame, or a slow-shutter figure by the sea. Let the audience supply identity and memory.

Keep: light as protagonist, people as the place it touches. Avoid: clear celebrity portraiture or performed emotion.

Ref · 07

Mac DeMarco

A carefully designed accident that still feels lived.

EverydayDiaryFriendsCheap Camera
Imaginary Lands5 / 5
Creative Direction

Casual memory, not retro style

VHS is a vehicle rather than the concept. The deeper quality is ordinary life caught without ceremony: “this was not made as a work”—even when carefully selected.

Visual Vocabulary

Consumer-image culture

  • VHS, DV, webcam, fisheye, handycam
  • Rooms, streets, cars and friends
  • Unposed human presence
  • Soft focus, color bleed and scan lines
Motion Language

Free, close and imperfect

The camera walks, sways, approaches and retreats without precision. Disorder becomes ease; technical correctness would remove its intimacy.

Rhythm

Diary fragments over composition

The edit follows moments worth retaining rather than formal coverage. Signal flicker—tracking, color shift, dropped frames and scan—keeps the image physically unstable.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Camera-born texture or careful emulation

Much of the character likely comes from consumer hardware. Without a real VHS/DV camera, After Effects treatments, Dehancer, grain, blur and chromatic aberration can recreate the signal language.

Technical1 / 5Aesthetic4 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

Record the life around the performance

Film cable setup, modular patching, train windows, hotel beds, breakfast, walking, studios, airports and floors. Do not make every frame beautiful; find the frames that feel true.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

The most immediately feasible reference

Pair two layers: an abstract archive of place, material and light; and a shared journal of ordinary life. Their tension makes the visual world belong specifically to Imaginary Lands.

Keep: the unperformed, everyday diary. Avoid: treating VHS as a fashionable filter with no personal content.

Ref · 08

The Marías

Intimacy appears only as a withheld nocturnal silhouette.

SilhouetteRed LightStillnessLow-Light Grain
Imaginary Lands4 / 5
Creative Direction

Intimacy that refuses disclosure

Two figures are present, but the image withholds facial detail. The emotional charge comes from proximity, darkness and the sense of a private moment that cannot be fully accessed.

Visual Vocabulary

Paired silhouettes and a red wound of light

  • Overlapping heads and shoulders
  • Near-black negative space
  • Localized red illumination
  • Low-light grain and compression
Motion Language

Almost still—surface remains alive

Physical movement is minimal. Subtle posture changes, exposure drift and grain fluctuation make the held portrait feel unstable rather than frozen.

Rhythm

One image carries the lyric

The frame persists while text and tiny luminance changes create temporal punctuation. Its stillness works as an emotional pause between more spatial or material passages.

Likely Production · Difficulty

Locked live action under extreme low light

Most likely a static or lightly handheld portrait, heavily underexposed, with a narrow red practical light or masked projection. Grain and compression may be partly camera-born and partly reinforced in post.

Technical1 / 5Aesthetic4 / 5
Reproduction Guidance

Reduce portraiture to a trace

Place two figures against darkness, expose for a small red light source and protect the silhouettes. Let the shot run. Add only restrained texture modulation; avoid revealing faces through lifted shadows.

iPhone Feasibility · IL Transfer

Very feasible with exposure locked low

Use it as a rare, intimate punctuation inside Imaginary Lands—two people implied rather than documented. It can bridge the private diary language of Mac DeMarco and the anonymous human energy of Emma.

Keep: proximity, withheld identity and red light. Avoid: turning the whole set into a lyric video or generic moody portrait.

03 · Instrument

Flicker is not an effect.

Treat it like a playable voice: a family of temporal modulations that lets the image breathe with the music without obeying every beat.

“The image flickers the way memory does.”

Alive, irregular, low-frequency—and never merely a flash cut.

Exposure breathing

Small luminance shifts suggest projector instability or a living sensor. Use slow, irregular curves rather than a metronomic pulse.

Texture flicker

Animate only grain density, compression or scan. The scene remains still while its surface continually renews.

Memory replacement

Interrupt image A with image B for 2–4 frames, then return. Rare use feels involuntary; repetition becomes a gimmick.

Light-leak sweep

A moving flare behaves as illumination, not a transition. Let it enter and leave the image without forcing a cut.

Club-light pulse

Capture real on-site light changes when possible. Their inconsistency is more convincing than a perfectly programmed strobe.

Signal instability

VHS tracking, color displacement, scan and dropped frames frame imperfection as a property of the medium.

04 · Production

An iPhone-first pipeline.

The phone is not a compromise here. It is a diary camera, a sensor for light and a practical tool for building a private visual archive over time.

01 · Capture

Shoot lived fragments

10–15 second clips. Hold longer than feels necessary. Capture 60 fps when slow motion is useful; preserve 24 or 30 fps for natural handheld immediacy.

02 · Archive

Organize by motif

Water, Windows, Paris, Taipei, Tokyo, Trees, Stone, Faces, Fog, Maps, Sky, Shadow, Reflection, Transit and Rooms.

03 · Select

Find the accident

Choose clips for light, ambiguity and emotional residue—not sharpness or coverage. Ten minutes of capture may yield thirty seconds.

04 · Treat

Change time’s surface

Blur, bloom, grain, flicker, long opacity blends, double exposure and a tightly restricted palette. Apply only what the source asks for.

05 · Perform

Export breathing layers

Prepare long loops and one-shot moments for Resolume. Map flicker or brightness loosely to musical density; preserve asynchronous drift.

What to film

Ordinary material with latent atmosphere

  • Water surfaces
  • Window reflections
  • Train platforms
  • Fogged glass
  • Hands and shoulders
  • Cable setup
  • Escalators
  • Roads and wires
  • Hotel rooms
  • Sea and cloud
What to protect

Imperfections that carry truth

  • High-ISO noise
  • Underexposure
  • Motion blur
  • Soft focus
  • Compression
  • Camera drift
  • Color bleed
  • Obstruction
  • Long pauses
  • Accidental light
05 · Visual Bible

The Imaginary Lands grammar.

A compact set of decisions that can guide filming, editing, AI use, collaboration and live performance.

Subjects

  • Shared memory
  • City and landscape archive
  • Natural phenomena
  • Anonymous human trace
  • Sculptural objects

Motion

  • Slow drift
  • Natural or physical movement
  • Long holds
  • Rare weighted cuts
  • Asynchronous breathing

Texture

  • Film grain and halation
  • Fog, glass and defocus
  • VHS / DV signal damage
  • Bloom and compression
  • Texture changing over time

Restraint

  • No compulsory beat sync
  • No constant scene changes
  • No generic AI spectacle
  • No beauty in every frame
  • No cleaning every defect
Do not make the image constantly change. Make it remain alive.
